crime_highlights: He coerced them through threats, violence and property destruction.
He broke the nose of one of his victims and fractured the rib of the other.
These offences had significant, long-lasting effects on the complainants.
rationale_highlights: The sentencing judge recognized that systemic discrimination had impacted the appellant deeply and contributed to him not graduating from high school and accruing a criminal record dating back to 1995.
it is important for the criminal justice system to recognize the link between systemic issues and certain types of criminal behaviour
The sentencing judge recognized the disadvantages faced by the appellant, including his experience with anti-Black racism and his need for rehabilitation.
note: Appeal decision; court says factors recognized but balanced against denunciation.

crime_highlights: The appellant was carrying two loaded firearms, both of which had oversized magazines, and a substantial amount of fentanyl when he fled from police.
He engaged in a dangerous high-speed car chase before fleeing on foot through a residential neighbourhood.
One of the guns discharged when he lost his balance in the backyard of a residence
rationale_highlights: The sentencing judge carefully considered an enhanced pre-sentence report focusing on the appellant’s family context and the impacts of systemic racism.

the appellant’s reduced moral culpability as a result of the social context in which he grew up had to be tempered by the need to protect the public, the appellant’s flagrant recidivism, and the gravity of his offences
note: Short appeal endorsement; rationale passage is brief.

crime_highlights: he stole a vehicle belonging to two people
The appellant entered the couple’s vehicle and put it in drive as the woman struggled to stop him.
The woman fell out of the vehicle as the appellant drove away and sustained serious injuries, including facial fractures, a deep head laceration, and a mild traumatic brain injury.
rationale_highlights: the sentencing judge expressly noted that she was taking into account “the obvious applicability of the Gladue features in this case” as a mitigating factor
note: Very brief Gladue treatment; no description of offender's history.
